name: Thirty-Five Films, Five Continents: A Viewer's Passport
description: A watch list that travels from Tokyo to Dakar to Mumbai to Rio, with the films that shaped how the world tells stories on screen and why each matters.

checkpoints.name: Silents to sound
checkpoints.note: Big studios and bold voices from Germany and the United States prove that film can be both mass entertainment and serious art, and after the war Italian neorealism takes the camera into the streets.

checkpoints.name: The postwar boom
checkpoints.note: Japan, India, Sweden and France send films abroad, and festivals make directors like Kurosawa, Ray and Bergman known across the world, while Hitchcock works at his peak in Hollywood.

checkpoints.name: Breaking the rules
checkpoints.note: New waves, anti-colonial stories and a science-fiction epic push cinema into new ground.

checkpoints.name: Auteurs and blockbusters
checkpoints.note: Directors gain freedom, Bombay makes action epics and Hollywood finds the summer hit, while African directors build their own cinema.

checkpoints.name: Cinema without borders
checkpoints.note: Animation, martial arts, drama from Brazil to Korea and Hong Kong reach audiences everywhere, and a Korean film wins the top Oscar.
